Patch 0.22.3 (Starter-route map priority and visual ordering)

  • Starter route priority: Quest Giver and Forge now draw first in the town route so the most important first-session stops stand out immediately.
  • Shared wayfinding order: world map and minimap both prioritize the same starter route instead of drifting between different service orders.
  • Visual emphasis: Quest and Forge markers now get stronger visual treatment so the first objective path reads faster at a glance.
  • Regression coverage: Added tests around town map ordering, minimap starter-route ordering, and version / patch-notes presentation for the 0.22.3 slice.

Patch 0.22.2 (First-step copy consistency and quest-funnel clarity)

  • Same next step everywhere: Start-screen copy, the objectives panel, and town onboarding now all point you to the Quest Giver by the Forge instead of drifting between vague phrases.
  • Map and journal handoff: First-session guidance now explicitly calls out World Map (M) and Journal (J) together so the next action is easier to recover after loading in.
  • Cleaner starter funnel: New players now get a more direct start-screen explanation of class pick -> town -> Quest Giver -> first quest flow.
  • Regression coverage: Added tests around start-flow wording, starter-town objective wording, and version / patch-notes presentation for the 0.22.2 slice.

Patch 0.22.1 (Starter-town wayfinding and service prompts)

  • Quest Giver prompt: Hovering the Quest Giver now tells first-session players exactly that this is where they pick up the first quest.
  • Town service hover hints: Forge, Stash, and Vendor / Repair now explain what they are for instead of just saying "interact".
  • Overworld re-entry onboarding: Returning to town refreshes the objective panel immediately so the starter funnel does not wait on a later quest packet.
  • Regression coverage: Added tests around overworld onboarding refresh, town hover hints, and version / patch-notes presentation for the new 0.22.1 patch.

Patch 0.22.0 (First-session onboarding and start-screen clarity)

  • First Steps panel: The login screen now explains the immediate path for both returning players and first-time characters instead of dumping you into a blank decision wall.
  • Smarter enter-world guidance: Logging into an existing character now shifts the start-screen copy toward resuming your run, opening quests, and using the tracker to find your next stop.
  • Clearer new-player funnel: Fresh accounts now get explicit character-creation guidance before entering the world, including what happens right after class selection.
  • Class role blurbs: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, and Cleric now each get a short role description so picking a class is less blind.
  • Regression coverage: Added tests around start-screen onboarding copy, login-state transitions, version presentation, and patch-notes history so the 0.22 entry path stays locked down.

Patch 0.21.5 (Closeout stability and HUD sanity)

  • Safer instance transitions: Entering or leaving dungeons now respects the shared scene-group boundaries instead of relying on broad scene cleanup that could disturb unrelated runtime state.
  • Dynamic scene ownership cleanup: Remote player meshes and transient instance content now clear through the render system's explicit ownership paths, making transition behavior easier to reason about and less brittle.
  • HUD update sanity pass: Core HUD state like health, mana, XP, and cooldown overlays now avoids unnecessary re-renders when nothing visible actually changed.
  • World map throttling: The world map no longer redraws every render frame while hidden, cutting wasted UI work during normal play.
  • Regression coverage: Added focused tests around instance-transition scene ownership and render-time HUD throttling so these closeout fixes stay locked in.

Patch 0.21.4 (Dungeon/menu/game-feel polish)

  • Dungeon portal UX: The dungeon menu now behaves like a cleaner modal with reliable header close, footer close, backdrop close, and Escape handling.
  • Respec modal polish: The respec flow follows the same close behavior so dismiss actions feel consistent instead of brittle.
  • Less accidental text selection: Menu/window chrome is now non-selectable while inputs still preserve normal text selection where typing/editing matters.
  • Sharper shadows: World shadows now use higher-resolution soft shadow settings and more stable follow behavior so buildings, fences, and thin shapes read more like the objects casting them.
  • Bigger jump feel: Ctrl+click jumps now have a more exaggerated arc, stronger airborne presentation, and more satisfying landing feedback.
  • Landing impact: Jump landings now kick up a richer dust burst and apply a small camera punch to make touchdown feel heavier.

Patch 0.21.3 (Asset pack caching finished for this release line)

  • Cached version visibility: Every downloadable pack now shows its Cached version directly in settings so it is obvious what is stored on this device.
  • Service-worker metadata: Cached pack versions now stay in sync whether assets are warmed directly or through the live service-worker path.
  • At-a-glance state badges: Packs now surface clear labels for Current, Outdated, Partial, Downloading, and not-yet-cached states.
  • Update Cached Assets: There is now a one-click maintenance action to refresh every pack you already keep on the device, without forcing unnecessary first-time downloads for packs you never chose.
  • Finished cache management pass: Keep Assets on This Device now covers recommended downloads, stale refreshes, cached version visibility, state badges, selective updates, and cache clearing in one complete flow.

Patch 0.19 (Passive Talents: Persistence & UX)

  • Passive Talents: Added a ranked passive talent system (0/5 per talent) that upgrades abilities rather than raw stat sticks.
  • Skill Tree UI: Added Skills / Talents tabs inside the K menu and a clearer talent points header showing available / total (spent).
  • Spec-Focused Talents: Talent list now only shows Mastery/Technique entries relevant to your currently selected branch (A/B/C).
  • Networking Fix (Critical): Fixed talents not replicating to clients by ensuring player state copies include talent ranks and talent points during broadcasts.
  • Server Authority: Talent points are derived from level and spent ranks (1 point per 5 levels) and validated server-side on unlock/reset.
  • Persistence & Migration: Talent ranks are saved/loaded reliably; legacy unlocked_talents data migrates safely and canonicalizes IDs (e.g. CLR_1 -> CLR_01) to prevent invisible/ignored ranks.
  • Responsiveness: Talent rank-ups and resets update immediately in UI (optimistic), then reconcile against server-confirmed state.
  • Mobile UX: Skill tree window is more usable on smaller screens (responsive sizing/layout).

Patch 0.18 (Protobuf State Streaming)

  • Networking: State updates now stream as protobuf frames (EDPB header + versioning) for lower bandwidth and CPU overhead.
  • Compatibility: Removed legacy gzip+JSON state update mode; client and server must both be updated to 0.18+.
  • Combat Visuals: Remote enemy attack animations now sync to damage events to prevent “running while hitting” desync.
  • Browser Fix: Protobuf JS runtime now loads reliably in the browser without resolving protobufjs/minimal as an ES module.
  • Tooling: Improved proto generation script so regenerating keeps the browser-safe protobuf module behavior.

Patch 0.17c (Animation & Sync Fixes)

  • Animation Fixes:
    • Cleric Spirit Guardians: Fixed spirits not disappearing and animation staying stuck on Attack after spell expires.
    • Ability Animations: All class abilities now properly return to Idle animation after casting completes.
    • Animation Cleanup: Added proper memory disposal for spirit visual effects.
  • Delta Sync Fixes:
    • Hotbar Icons: Fixed ability icons disappearing from the hotbar after login.
    • Skill Tree: Fixed specialization selection not working in the K menu.
    • Full State Sync: Delta updates now properly sync skills, equipment, inventory, XP, level, and gold.
